source_title: World of Warcraft Forever Name Reservation is Running Into Some Issues
source_excerpt:
Starting on October 27, Blizzard allowed World of Warcraft: Forever players to reserve character names ahead of launch, but many are running into bugs and issues. Blizzard's new game had been leaked and rumored for months before its official release as "Classic Plus," a sort of hybrid between the retail version of World of Warcraft and the vanilla experience from over 20 years ago. The game was finally announced at BlizzCon, with a restricted-access beta that went live in mid-September and closed just a week ago. Now, World of Warcraft: Forever is launching in just a few days.
Despite the game launching on November 4, Blizzard is still making multiple changes to the final build. For example, after a major balance pass on most racial abilities and passives, World of Warcraft: Forever is nerfing the most played class in the game ahead of launch . This also comes with a group-wide change that will inevitably impact endgame activities with multiple players. More similar patches may come in the next few days, but hopefully, the name reservation process will be fixed by then.
World of Warcraft: Forever's Name Reservation System is Officially Bugged
WoW: Forever 's name reservation system went live on Tuesday and had a rough start, with the automatic name filter being overly strict in applying rules, but issues seem to continue even after an official fix. Fans couldn't save their changes and instead got an error message saying "Character creation timed out," and then were unable to reserve their chosen names. This has since been partly fixed, with Blizzard reporting through Community Manager Kaivax that non-profane names and names not identical to major Warcraft characters like Sylvanas or Malfurion were blocked, but others should go through.
Many players are still reporting issues on social media, though, and trying to reserve names for mains or alts in World of Warcraft: Forever can yield frustrating results due to strict mature language filters or due to names even remotely similar to NPCs, such as with the word "nurse," as reported by a fan named Nursejoy. "Doctor" and "goblin" also seem to be off-limits. Essentially, all sorts of named NPCs with a title in their name may be filtered out for the rest of the week if Blizzard doesn't deploy another fix, and in the worst-case scenario, the bug could carry over into launch as well. Hopefully, players can reserve the names they want before launch, though, as this is a paid feature that comes from the Skyborne Pack that also granted beta access.

World of Warcraft fans aren't happy with housing and cosmetic microtransactions that popped up suddenly in the store for Halloween, so seeing that a paid service doesn't work fully may cause further controversy. Furthermore, some names that should have been caught by the filter weren't, which makes the system even more problematic.
With Blizzard nerfing World of Warcraft: Forever 's best race before launch, only to then make sure Humans stay on top of the DPS charts, some players are already calling this "Alliance favoritism." Since one of the game's core ideas is to be the ultimate social MMO, having issues with character names a week before launch can be quite the headache.
